clue.text: Often turned over with resolution on January 1

definitions.text: Often turned over with resolution on January 1

parts.words: Often turned over with resolution on January 1
parts.note: reads like a page being flipped, but means the fresh start people resolve on at New Year

explanation.definitionFit: To turn over this is an idiom for starting to behave better, typical of New Year resolutions.

clue.text: Mr Runyan upset one of those wandering the desert

definitions.text: one of those wandering the desert

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down, i.e. reads it backwards

parts.note: Damon Runyon was an American writer of Broadway stories

explanation.surface: A writer is put out by a desert wanderer.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad is a member of a wandering people, often in deserts.

clue.text: The Magi seem upset in victory

indicators.note: in says the rearranged word goes inside the other piece

parts.note: a win is a victory

indicators.note: upset says the word seem is knocked into a different order

explanation.surface: The three kings look troubled in triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' makes ISEME from SEEM, which goes into WIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magi who visited the infant Jesus are traditionally called the three wise men.

clue.text: She follows one sort of track in pantomime

definitions.text: She follows one sort of track in pantomime

parts.words: She follows one sort of track in pantomime
parts.note: a cinder track is a sort of running track; this girl's name follows that word in the title of a famous pantomime

explanation.walkthrough: Cinderella is a classic British Christmas pantomime: the name after CINDER (a cinder track) is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This girl's name completes the pantomime title after the word for a cinder track.

clue.text: Stocking filler

parts.note: usually a small gift, but here the one who fills the stockings

explanation.definitionFit: Santa Claus is the figure who fills children's stockings with presents on Christmas Eve.

clue.text: The embodiment of a mince pie, in my opinion

indicators.note: to mince is to chop up finely, so the word pie is cut up and rearranged

parts.note: 'to me' is a way of saying in my opinion

explanation.surface: Someone declares a mince pie to be the very essence of Christmas fare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mince' looks like part of the food, but it signals rearranging PIE into EPI.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfect example or embodiment of something is its epitome; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: His Christmas present was one of three

definitions.text: His Christmas present was one of three

parts.words: His Christmas present was one of three
parts.note: not a gift: the Ghost of Christmas Present was one of the three spirits visiting this miser in Dickens

explanation.walkthrough: In Dickens's A Christmas Carol, the miser is visited by ghosts of Christmas Past, Present and Yet to Come.
explanation.definitionFit: The miser in A Christmas Carol is visited by three ghosts, including the Ghost of Christmas Present.

clue.text: Vessel that's ideal for the party?

definitions.meaning: a ship that cuts through polar ice
something that breaks the ice, getting guests talking

explanation.surface: A ship is said to be perfect for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a ship that clears frozen seas, and also an opening game or remark that eases social awkwardness.

clue.text: Mince pies to include a number of drugs

indicators.note: to include says the rearranged letters take in another piece
to mince is to chop up, so the letters are chopped and rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to put a few drugs into mince pies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mince pies' looks like the festive food, but 'Mince' is the anagram signal, and the 'to' of 'to include' is also fodder before the A goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Opiates are drugs derived from opium, so the plural names a number of drugs.

clue.text: Turn me over — that's better!

definitions.note: an exclamation; the answer is a past participle meaning corrected

indicators.note: turn says the word me is turned round

parts.note: something over has ended

explanation.surface: A plea to be rolled over for comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: Emended text has been corrected and improved, so it is better.

clue.text: Stole time off — for Christmas?

indicators.note: off suggests the letters have gone bad or are out of their usual order

explanation.surface: Someone took a crafty kiss, or time away from work, at Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges the letters of STOLE TIME. The definition is loose: a plant hung up for Christmas, under which kisses are stolen.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig of this plant is a traditional Christmas decoration, hung up for kissing under.

clue.text: The best part of the goose, literally

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A diner names their favourite bit of the Christmas goose.
explanation.definitionFit: An elite is the best or choicest group, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Character dragged up at this time of the year?

definitions.text: Character dragged up at this time of the year?

parts.words: Character dragged up at this time of the year?
parts.note: dragged up suggests a badly raised child, but means a man dressed in drag for a Christmas pantomime

explanation.walkthrough: British Christmas pantomimes feature a comic older woman played by a man in drag.
explanation.definitionFit: The pantomime role of a comic old woman is traditionally played by a male actor in drag.

clue.text: Well-known way in which Christmas is enjoyed

definitions.text: way in which Christmas is enjoyed
definitions.meaning: the festival is marked with festivities, i.e. observed with a party

explanation.surface: Christmas is a famous festival, enjoyed in a well-known way.
explanation.definitionFit: Famous people are described as celebrated, and a festival kept with parties has been celebrated.

clue.text: Source of present-day jingles

parts.note: suggests modern advertising tunes, but means the ringing on Santa's transport on the day presents arrive

explanation.definitionFit: Bells on a sleigh jingle, and Santa's sleigh brings presents on Christmas Day.

clue.text: Noel with balloons and chains, initially well turned out, as a whole

indicators.note: turned out suggests smartly dressed, but here the letters are turned about into a new order
initially takes just the opening letter of each of the words balloons and chains

explanation.surface: A Christmas room decorated with balloons and paper chains looks well turned out overall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives B and C, which join NOEL; 'well turned out' rearranges NOELBC.
explanation.definitionFit: This French phrase means all together or as a single unit, matching as a whole.

clue.text: Unusually pleased to have passed by

indicators.note: unusually says the letters are set out in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Someone is oddly glad to have gone past.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that has elapsed has gone by or passed, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Like the winter weather for a ruler?

definitions.meaning: more wet, as weather tends to be in winter

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether winter weather suits a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Winter weather is wetter, comparatively speaking, and Prince Rainier was the long-reigning ruler of Monaco.

clue.text: Understanding how to tap the wine

parts.note: to rap is to tap or knock
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Advice on broaching a cask of wine knowledgeably.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapport is a close mutual understanding between people.

clue.text: Middle Easterner playing solitaire, but not having to?

indicators.note: playing says the letters of solitaire are rearranged
but not having says a word is removed from those letters before rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone from the region plays patience but wonders if they must.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove T and O from SOLITAIRE and rearrange what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Israel is a person from the Middle East.

clue.text: Winter transport is murder, they say

indicators.note: they say means the word is to be heard spoken, not read

parts.note: to slay is to murder

explanation.surface: Someone complains that getting about in winter is murder.
explanation.definitionFit: A sledge pulled by horses or reindeer is a classic means of winter travel.

clue.text: One too young to make Christmas dinner?

definitions.text: One too young to make Christmas dinner?

parts.words: One too young to make Christmas dinner?
parts.note: sounds like a child unable to cook, but is a young bird too small to be roasted

explanation.definitionFit: A young goose is too small to serve as the festive roast bird.

clue.text: Sounds of contentment about course for consumers

indicators.note: about means one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a cat's purrs are sounds of contentment
to course is to chase game, as with hounds

explanation.surface: Shoppers purr happily as they go about their Christmas buying.
explanation.definitionFit: Purchasers are buyers, and consumers are those who buy goods.

clue.text: Drink: knock it back as a starter

indicators.note: as a starter puts the word as at the front of the answer

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: back says the word it is read in reverse

explanation.surface: An instruction to down a drink as a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knock' only joins: 'knock it back' reads as gulping a drink, but 'back' turns IT into TI, and 'as a starter' puts AS first.
explanation.definitionFit: This sparkling Italian wine from Piedmont is a drink.

clue.text: Perfect cards came from me

parts.note: I is the speaker
the deal is the hand-out from which cards came

explanation.surface: A card player boasts that a flawless hand came from them.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically: 'I deal' means the cards come from me.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal means perfect, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Like to take one to a region where Jesus was born

parts.note: as means like, in comparisons
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An instruction to take someone to the Holy Land.
explanation.definitionFit: Bethlehem lies in western Asia, the continent where Jesus was born.

clue.text: Decorations have point for those that have eaten too much

definitions.text: those that have eaten too much

parts.note: OBEs are British honours, worn as decorations
E is east, a compass point

explanation.surface: Medals are awarded to people who overindulged at dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: An OBE (Order of the British Empire) is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: People who have eaten far too much become very fat, which this adjective describes.

clue.text: Cynthia takes a liking to alcohol

parts.note: Cynthia is a name for the Greek moon goddess Artemis, so stands for the moon
to take a shine to someone is to take a liking to them

explanation.surface: A woman called Cynthia develops a fondness for drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Illicitly distilled spirits, especially whisky, are called by this name.

clue.text: Toys provided for the children's party

definitions.meaning: custard-and-sponge desserts served at a party

explanation.surface: Toys are given out at a children's party.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who toys with things trifles with them, and trifle is a layered dessert at parties.

clue.text: Gave Len unusually good news for Christians!

indicators.note: unusually says the letters come out in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Len was handed some cheering news at Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Evangel means the gospel, literally good news, a word for the Christian message.
